cites.title: Aina Jurciņa
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. ‖ 10. | 58. | dessen Frau Anne | 38. / dessen Frau Anne | 21. / Tochter Anne | 5.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now. His wife Anne, 38; [Jahn's] wife Anne, 21; daughter Anne, 5.
cites.note: 1857 soul revision, family 10/58, XIX Gibboi farm: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth' (Jahn's son Mārcis, the farmer, head of the farm), 34½ at the last revision (1850), now 41½ (b. c. 1816); 'dessen Frau Anne', 38 (b. c. 1819). With them: his brothers 2. Jahn (35; wife Anne 21; son Marz b. 1855) and 3. Dahw (25½ in 1850, gone by 1857), and 'Tochter Anne', 5 (b. c. 1852), entered after Jahn's wife, so the page leaves open whether she is Mārcis's daughter or Jahn's. No Marija: Marija Gibboja (b. 1853) is 'Marri, 4' in the Rauguļi household of the other Marz Gibboi, 50 (image 16).
cites.why: Read at full size, both pages (Round 3). Mārcis, Jahn's son, 41½, is the Mārcis Ģibols b. 1816, son of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847), of Raimonds's tree: age and father agree. His wife Anne, 38, is the Anna b. 1819 whom the tree calls Anna Balodis (the surname is the tree's alone).
cites.as_recorded: Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth; dessen Frau Anne

Parents: farmer (Wirth) Peter Sirlak and his wife Mari née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: Mdf.[?] Anna Dutzmann[?]; Kn.[?] Jahn Karnicht[?] and his wife Kristine. Rauna Latvian baptisms 1890, no. 96.

cites.title: Pēteris Sirlaks
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 10.08.1847 Miršanas datums: 10.11.1896 … Tēva vārds: Mārcis … Kapsēta: Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi … Marija Sirlaka — Sieva — 00.00.1853 – 00.00.1925
cites.translation: Born 10 Aug 1847, died 10 Nov 1896; father's name Mārcis; cemetery Jaunrauna (Priekuļi parish); wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925
cites.note: Timenote gives Pēteris Sirlaks 10 Aug 1847 – 10 Nov 1896, son of Mārcis and Anna Sirlaks, buried in Jaunrauna cemetery (Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi). Wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925, NOT 1920 as in the 2015 tree. Children: Natalie 1875–1887, Ernestīne 1879, Mārtiņš 1884–1942, Dāvis 1886–1952, Kristīne 1888, Anna 1890 (the memoir's aunt Anna in Rīga), Augusts 1895. 1938 court notices (Valdības Vēstnesis) mention mortgages issued by a Pēteris Sirlaks, with inheritance shares under a 16 Apr 1915 division act going to Augusts, Ernestīne and Anna Sirlaks. Very likely the same family's farm, which would place the estate division in 1915. PROBABLE SOURCE OF THE 2015 DATES: MyHeritage 'Jurcins Web Site' by Māris Jurciņš (Latvia), whose public name index spells her 'Marija Sirlaka (Ģībojs)', 'Marija Gilboy' and 'Gibboja (Ģībojs)'. 'Gibboja' is exactly the 2015 tree's spelling. Peter emailed himself 'Sirlaks myheritage.com genealogy' on 2018-11-16. MyHeritage pages are behind an hCaptcha and were NOT opened. Marija's maiden name 'Ģībojs/Gibboja' should be verified in the Jaunrauna/Rauna church books.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] Both are user trees without a cited record, so they are derivative until checked against the Rauna/Jaunrauna registers (Raduraksti).

cites.translation: KALAMAZOO. On 19 February, in Lee Memorial hospital in the city of Dowagiac, Michigan, the agronomist Arvīds Danenbergs died after a collision between two cars. … His wife Elvīra, riding with him, was injured … Arvīds Danenbergs was born 17 January 1913 in Tukums. He earned an agronomist's degree in Latvia and a master's in agriculture in Germany. … After cremation a memorial service for A. Danenbergs was held on 4 March at 'Saulgrieži', Garezers … farewells were spoken by the deceased's wife's sister Mirdza Gailīte and daughters Līga Šūbacha (Schubach) and Ilze Bērziņa. … Mourned by his wife Elvīra (still in hospital), daughters, sons with families, brother Žanis in Latvia
cites.note: The Laiks and Latvija Amerikā obituaries (1996) say 'dzimis … Tukumā'.
cites.why: Two independent obituaries in the two main US Latvian papers agree; they name his wife Elvīra, his sister-in-law Mirdza Gailīte and his daughter Līga Schubach.

cites.title: Declaration of Intention No. 134, Arvids Danenbergs, Mercer County Common Pleas, Celina, Ohio, 14 Aug 1950
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: (5) I was born on Jan. 17, 1913 in Sturumuiza Latvia
cites.note: Gregorian date. The FamilySearch tree (LR39-9HZ) and the SSDI have 4 Jan 1913, which is the same day in the Julian (Old Style) calendar still used in Russian Courland in 1913 (a 13-day difference). The NUMIDENT, the Michigan death index, the declaration of intention and both obituaries all have 17 Jan. "Sturumuiza" is probably a manor/farm (muiža) name. Auce is the nearest town. Both fit Zemgale, where his father taught.
cites.why: Five independent US records agree on 17 Jan 1913, and the 4 Jan date is exactly the O.S. equivalent. The birthplace is self-reported, so only medium confidence on the place.

cites.title: Zudušie ASV: Miris Arvīds Danenbergs (in 'Ziņas un chronika')
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.locator: Daugavas Vanagu Mēnešraksts, Nr.2 (01.04.1996), section beginning p. 46
cites.quote: Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs, dzimis 1913.g. 17. janvārī Tukuma apriņķa Stūrmuižas pagastā. Pēc 2.Jelgavas valsts ģimnāzijas beigšanas studē Lauksaimniecības Akadēmijā Jelgavā, ko beidz ar agronoma grādu. Strādā Talsu agronomiskā birojā. 1941.g. no Sv. Jāņa baznīcas Cēsīs uzsāk kopīgu ģimenes dzīvi ar farmaceiti Elvīru Širlaku. 1944.g. Arvīds ar sievu, 2 gadus vecu dēlu Pēteri un sievas māti Emmu Širlaku dodas bēgļu gaitās uz Vāciju. Tur turpina izglītību Štutgartes—Hohenheimas agrikultūras augstkolā, kur iegūst mākstera grādu agronomijā. 1949.g. izceļo uz ASV. … Miris pēkšņā nāvē auto katastrofā 1996. g. 19. februārī, atstājot sievu Elvīru, trīs bērnus — Pēteri, Kalvi, Līgu, 3 mazbērnus ASV, brāli Žani un vairākus radus Latvijā. Pārpelnots un pelnu urna nosūtīta uz Latviju.
cites.translation: Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs, born 17 January 1913 in Stūrmuiža parish, Tukums district. After finishing the 2nd Jelgava State Gymnasium he studied at the Agricultural Academy in Jelgava, graduating as an agronomist. He worked at the Talsi agronomy bureau. In 1941, from St John's church in Cēsis, he began family life with the pharmacist Elvīra Širlaka [sic]. In 1944 Arvīds, his wife, their two-year-old son Pēteris and his wife's mother Emma Širlaka fled as refugees to Germany. There he continued his studies at the Stuttgart-Hohenheim agricultural college, earning a master's degree in agronomy. In 1949 he emigrated to the USA. … Died suddenly in a car accident on 19 February 1996, survived by his wife Elvīra, three children (Pēteris, Kalvis, Līga), 3 grandchildren in the USA, his brother Žanis and several relatives in Latvia. Cremated; the urn was sent to Latvia.
cites.note: 17 January is the New Style date; 4 January 1913 (Old Style) = 17 January 1913 (New Style), which reconciles the FamilySearch date 1913-01-04. Middle name Fricis. The 1983 jubilee note instead says "Vecauces pag." (Vecauce parish, Jelgava district), and the Laiks and Latvija Amerikā obituaries say "Tukumā", so the place is uncertain between Stūrmuiža (Tukums district) and Vecauce.
cites.why: Three independent exile-press notices give 17 Jan 1913; the parish differs between them (Stūrmuiža / Tukums / Vecauce). Identity is certain (wife Elvīra, children Pēteris, Kalvis, Līga).

cites.title: Mūsu jubilāri
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Arvīds Danenbergs, DV ap-bas Latvijas ciemā pie Garezerā valdes loc, 17. janv. atskatījās uz 70 mūža gadiem. Dzimis 1913. g. Vecauces pag. Beidzis LU lauksaimniecības fakultāti un strādāja par Talsu raj. agronomu. Ieradies ASV, 1949. g. viņš strādāja Ziemeļohaio lopu audzēšanas kooperatīvā, bet 1955. g. nopirka savu lauksaimniecību, ko turpina apsaimniekot.
cites.translation: Arvīds Danenbergs, board member of the DV branch in the Latvian village at Garezers, turned 70 on 17 January. Born 1913 in Vecauce parish. Graduated from the agricultural faculty of the University of Latvia and worked as the Talsi district agronomist. Arriving in the USA in 1949, he worked at a northern Ohio livestock-breeding co-operative, and in 1955 bought his own farm, which he still runs.
cites.note: 1983 jubilee note: born in Vecauces pagasts.
cites.why: 70th-birthday note, matching the memoir and the Tiffin, Ohio photo-back.

cites.title: Household of Arwids F Danenbergs, Liberty Township, Mercer, Ohio
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: 136 No No Danenbergs, Arwids F Head W M 37 Mar Latvia … WK … 70 Farm Hand Farm P
cites.note: 1950 census, ED 54-34, sheet 16, lines 14-22, dwelling 136, enumerator Bernice Fetters. Head, 37, farm hand, born Latvia. Household: Elvira A (wife, 38), Peter V (son, 7, b. Latvia), Liga (daughter, 3, b. Germany), Kalvis V (son, 3, b. Germany), Emma Sirlaks (mother-in-law, 65, widowed, b. Latvia), Witolds Balks (brother-in-law, 29, farm hand), Biruta Z Balks (sister-in-law, 30), Ilze Balks (niece, 4, b. Germany). Line 30 on the same sheet, the next dwelling but three, is HAWK, Robert M., 25, farmer: very likely the "Hawk farm" sponsor in the memoir. So the first US home was in Mercer County (Rockford/Celina), not Seneca County (Tiffin). Tiffin comes later. In April 1950 Mirdza addressed her mother "c/o E. Sirlaks - D. R. Smalley Farms, Rockford, Ohio" (see the Detroit card below).

cites.note: Sailed from Bremerhaven on the "Gen. Blatchford" (USAT General R. M. Blatchford, a DP transport) and was admitted under the name "Arvids Danenburgs". cites.why: Three declarations from the same family agree. This confirms the memoir's 'Boston, July 1949' and adds the ship, the day and the A-numbers.

facts.value: WWI draft card: age 25, born 12 September 1891 at Comanche, Texas; natural-born citizen; farmer for F. W. McCauley, El Portal; no dependents; single; tall, slender, dark blue eyes, light brown hair. Signed 'Chas. Hall'.
Draft-lottery list printed in the Merced paper: '107 Chas. Henry Hall, El Portal.'
Draft serial no. 107, order no. 10. Examined by the Mariposa Local Exemption Board: 'Passed and No Exemption Claimed'.
On the corrected list of men called for service (order no. 10). The same article says all single men were denied exemption, which fits the draft card's 'single'.

Inducted with the first Mariposa contingent: he left Wednesday 19 Sep 1917 for training at Camp Lewis (Pierce Co., WA), home of the 91st Division. This independently corroborates the VA master index card (FamilySearch Q5GN-L53Z): '316 MP / 91st Div'.

Private, service no. 2274478. Roster at midnight 30 Sep 1918, page 2, Privates no. 70, with no remark: he was already in the company on 1 Sep, while other men are marked 'Joined Co 6th' etc. The 31 Oct 1918 roster of the same company lists him again: '57. Hall, Charles H. 2274478', no remark (Roll…

Transferred out of the 48th Co., 12th Bn., 166th Depot Brigade on 11 Nov 1918. Listed under 'LOSSES FOR THE MONTH OF NOVEMBER', Privates no. 20. The destination is not stated; every loss on the page reads 'Trans Nov. [day]'. Indexed by FS as a 31 Dec 1918 roster. OCR misreads the serial as…

facts.place: Clark County, Washington, Washington, United States
facts.value: Private, roster at midnight 31 Dec 1918, page 4, no. 63, with no remark. The serial is a blurred carbon reading '2,274,47[8]'. The next line, '64. Hall, Ralph E. 880,443 / Jnd. for duty Dec. 28/18', is another man. This places him at Vancouver Barracks seven weeks after he left Camp Lewis.

facts.place: Vancouver, Clark County, Washington, United States
facts.value: VA Master Index card: Pvt, 'B H Co A 316 MP' (the 316th Train Headquarters and Military Police, 91st Division, the Camp Lewis division of West Coast draftees, home in Apr 1919); service no. 2 274 478; born 9/12/90; discharged 4/ /19; died 9-12-61 (stamped 9-20-61). Claim file XC 198 015; A 4 421…

Separated from Susan by 1930: she heads the household and is 'married' in 1930, 'widowed' in 1940 and 'separated' in 1950. He was not found in the 1930, 1940 or 1950 census, and his death was not found.

Is he the WWI registrant Charles Henry Hall, b. 12 Sep 1891 Comanche TX (El Portal CA, 1917)? Probably yes. (1) The VA card links a Charles Henry Hall, b. 12 Sep [1890], to Vancouver WA and to a 91st Division unit; (2) there are only two Texas-born Charles H. Halls b. 1890-91 in the 1920 census:…

Other Texas-born Charles Halls b. 1890-92 seen in 1920 (FamilySearch 1920 census, birthplace Texas, b. 1890-91): Charly B. Hall, single, Fresno CA (the only other West Coast one); Charles M. Hall, single, McClain Co. OK (with parents Walter C. and Mary E.); Charlie Hall, married, Van Zandt Co. TX…

cites.title: Young Men to Leave for Service Next Week, Mariposa Gazette, 15 Sep 1917
cites.repository: California Digital Newspaper Collection
cites.quote: They will go to Camp Lewis for training ... Wednesday, Sept. 19th.—Walter A. Grace, William Pierce, Charles 11 Hall, William R. Bonds, Andrew Horgan.
cites.note: Inducted with the first Mariposa contingent: he left Wednesday 19 Sep 1917 for training at Camp Lewis (Pierce Co., WA), home of the 91st Division. This independently corroborates the VA master index card (FamilySearch Q5GN-L53Z): '316 MP / 91st Div'.
cites.why: Same 19 Sep group as Grace, Pierce, Bonds and Horgan, who were nos. 5, 8, 20 and 22 in the order list. Hall was no. 10, so the El Portal man is certain. [DNA evidence (private)] It also explains how a Mariposa man ended up in SW Washington (Vancouver).

cites.title: Roster of 48th Company, 12th Battalion, 166th Depot Brigade, at midnight September 30th, 1918
cites.repository: NARA, via FamilySearch
cites.quote: Roster of 48th Company, 12th Battalion, 166th Depot Brigade, at midnight September 30th, 1918. ... 70. Hall, Charles H. 2274478
cites.note: Private, service no. 2274478. Roster at midnight 30 Sep 1918, page 2, Privates no. 70, with no remark: he was already in the company on 1 Sep, while other men are marked 'Joined Co 6th' etc. The 31 Oct 1918 roster of the same company lists him again: '57. Hall, Charles H. 2274478', no remark (Roll 2105, image 3:1:3QHV-J3DB-J94D-9, record 4T56-FV2M).
cites.why: Service number 2274478 is identical to the VA Master Index card's (Q5GN-L53Z). The draft board sent him to Camp Lewis on 19 Sep 1917.

cites.title: 48th Co., 12th Bn., 166th D.B., Camp Lewis, Wash., Dec. [4?], 1918: Losses for the month of November
cites.repository: NARA, via FamilySearch
cites.quote: LOSSES FOR THE MONTH OF NOVEMBER: ... 20. Hall, Charles H. 2274478 Trans Nov. 11th
cites.note: Transferred out of the 48th Co., 12th Bn., 166th Depot Brigade on 11 Nov 1918. Listed under 'LOSSES FOR THE MONTH OF NOVEMBER', Privates no. 20. The destination is not stated; every loss on the page reads 'Trans Nov. [day]'. Indexed by FS as a 31 Dec 1918 roster. OCR misreads the serial as 2874476; on the image it reads 2274478.
cites.why: Same name and service number 2274478, in the same company as the Sep/Oct rosters.

cites.title: Roster of Detachment Medical Department, Post Hospital, Vancouver Barracks, Washington at midnight Dec. 31, 1918
cites.repository: NARA, via FamilySearch
cites.quote: Roster of Detachment Medical Department, Post Hospital, Vancouver Barracks, Washington at midnight Dec. 31, 1918 ... 63. Hall, Charles H. 2,274,47[8]
cites.note: Private, roster at midnight 31 Dec 1918, page 4, no. 63, with no remark. The serial is a blurred carbon reading '2,274,47[8]'. The next line, '64. Hall, Ralph E. 880,443 / Jnd. for duty Dec. 28/18', is another man. This places him at Vancouver Barracks seven weeks after he left Camp Lewis.
cites.why: Same name and initial. [DNA evidence (private)] He left the 166th D.B. on 11 Nov 1918, and the VA card reads 'Vancouver Wash'. The last digit is blurred, so the serial is not a clean reading.

cites.title: Hall, Charles Henry, Vancouver Wash, b. 9/12/90
cites.repository: VA, via FamilySearch
cites.quote: HALL CHARLES HENRY | Pvt B H Co A 316 MP | Vancouver Wash | Sn 2 274 478 | Born 9/12/90 | Died 9-12-61 | Dis 4/ /19 | XC 198 015
cites.note: VA Master Index card: Pvt, 'B H Co A 316 MP' (the 316th Train Headquarters and Military Police, 91st Division, the Camp Lewis division of West Coast draftees, home in Apr 1919); service no. 2 274 478; born 9/12/90; discharged 4/ /19; died 9-12-61 (stamped 9-20-61). Claim file XC 198 015; A 4 421 289; T 1 999 247; R 24 241; Ct. 3 776 663. Address: Vancouver Wash.
cites.why: Charles Henry Hall, with a Vancouver, WA address, born 12 Sep (the same day and month as the Comanche draft card's 12 Sep 1891). A Mariposa Co., CA draftee of 1917 would normally have gone to Camp Lewis and the 91st Division. Our man was in Vancouver by Jan 1919 (daughter's birth). Discharge in Apr 1919 is after Margaret's birth in Jan 1919, which fits a soldier stationed nearby (Camp Lewis / Vancouver Barracks). The birth year is 1890, not 1891, and the card does not name Susan.

cites.note: Separated from Susan by 1930: she heads the household and is 'married' in 1930, 'widowed' in 1940 and 'separated' in 1950. He was not found in the 1930, 1940 or 1950 census, and his death was not found.
cites.why: The 1950 'separated' suggests he was still alive in 1950 and that the 1940 'widowed' was a social answer, but this is an inference.

cites.title: Charles H Hall, Pilot Point, Denton, Texas
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: Charles H Hall | Married | 1920 Pilot Point, Denton, Texas | Birth: 1891 Texas (household: Cora A b. 1897, Alma M 1913, James O 1915, Charles H 1916)
cites.note: Is he the WWI registrant Charles Henry Hall, b. 12 Sep 1891 Comanche TX (El Portal CA, 1917)? Probably yes. (1) The VA card links a Charles Henry Hall, b. 12 Sep [1890], to Vancouver WA and to a 91st Division unit; (2) there are only two Texas-born Charles H. Halls b. 1890-91 in the 1920 census: ours (Vancouver) and one in Pilot Point, Denton Co., TX, who was married with a son Charles H. b. 1916 (MHT4-91L), so he cannot be the single man of Jun 1917 in California; (3) no WWII 1942 card for a Charles H. Hall b. 12 Sep 1890/91 (collection 1861144), and no 1930/1940 census entry that could be him with another family.
cites.why: Three independent circumstantial links. None names Susan. The 1919 discharge paper or the VA claim file XC 198 015 would settle it.

cites.translation: Born 4 April, 3 p.m.; baptised 13 April. No. 134. Neuhof, Lower Vīstuči: Dawid Sirlak. Parents: farmer Peter Sirlak and his wife Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmer Dahw Bitte; farmer Mahrz Sirnis and his wife Lihse. Baptised at home by farmer Dahw Gudre; confirmed 10 August by Pastor [Sirne?] in church.
cites.note: Born 4 Apr 1886 Julian (= 16 Apr 1886 Gregorian), 3 p.m.; baptised at home 13 Apr 1886 by farmer Dahw Gudre, confirmed (bestätigt) in church 10 Aug 1886 by the pastor [Sirne?]. Legitimate son of farmer (Wirth) Peter Sirlak and his wife Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmer Dahw Bitte; farmer Mahrz Sirnis and his wife Lihse. Same parents and farm as Mārtiņš Vilhelms (1883 no. 324), so the two are full brothers. The relative's tree date 4 Apr 1886 is the Julian date.

cites.title: Aina Jurciņa
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.title: Mūsu jubilāri
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Elvīrai Danenbergai, dzim. Sirlaka, piepildījās 75 mūža gadi. Dzimusi 1912. g. 9. janv. Rīgā. Skolas gadus pavadījusi Cēsīs. 1941. g. beigusi LU Ķīmijas fakultātes Farmācijas nod. ar maģistra grādu. Strādājusi Rīgā un vairākās provinces aptiekās. ASV apmetusies Ohio, un kopā ar vīru agr. Arvīdu uzaudzināja 2 dēlus un meitu. Strādāja par farmaceiti Tiffin Ohio. Pārceļoties uz Mičigenu, dzīvo savā farmā Garezera tuvumā.
cites.translation: Elvīra Danenberga, née Sirlaka, turned 75. Born 9 Jan 1912 in Rīga. Spent her school years in Cēsis. In 1941 graduated from the Pharmacy Section of the Chemistry Faculty of the University of Latvia with a master's degree. Worked in Rīga and several provincial pharmacies. In the USA settled in Ohio and with her husband, the agronomist Arvīds, raised 2 sons and a daughter. Worked as a pharmacist in Tiffin, Ohio. Moving to Michigan, she lives on her farm near Garezers.
cites.note: Schooling in Cēsis. In 1941 she graduated from the Pharmacy Section of the Chemistry Faculty of the University of Latvia with a master's degree ("maģistra grāds"). She worked in Rīga and several provincial pharmacies, and in the USA as a pharmacist in Tiffin, Ohio. 9 January is confirmed by DV Milwaukee birthday lists for 2002, 2003 and 2006.
cites.why: 75th-birthday note names her maiden name and husband Arvīds; [DNA evidence (private)] The day is repeated in three later notices.

cites.title: Rīga St Martin Latvian congregation 1912, births and baptisms no. 82
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 3036, apr. 4, l. 68, image 15 (right page, bottom)
cites.quote: 1911 Декабря двадцать седьмого (27) 7 ч. веч. | 1912 Февраля девятнадцатаго (19) | № 82 | Эльвира Антонія (Elvira Antonie). Род. торговецъ Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Сирлакъ (Sirlak) ев. лют. вѣр. и его жена Эмма, ур. Смукулъ ев. лют. вѣроиспов. Воспр.: Давидъ Сирлакъ, хозяинъ; Анна Смукулъ, дѣв.; Эрнестина Сирлакъ, дѣвица. Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]
cites.translation: Born 27 December 1911, 7 p.m.; baptised 19 February 1912. No. 82. Elvira Antonie. Parents: trader Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Lutheran, and his wife Emma née Smukul, Ev.-Lutheran. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. Baptised [in …] by Pastor Hilde[?].
cites.note: Born 27 Dec 1911 Julian (= 9 Jan 1912 Gregorian) at 7 p.m.; baptised 19 Feb 1912 Julian (= 3 Mar 1912 Gregorian). Full baptismal name Elvira Antonie. Father: trader (торговецъ) Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Luth.; mother: his wife Emma née Smukul (the ending '-улъ' written over a struck-out ending), Ev.-Luth. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner (хозяинъ) [= her uncle Dāvis]; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. The last line, in another hand, reads roughly 'Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]' — baptised [at …] by Pastor Hilde[?]; place uncertain. Entry no. 82 sits among March baptisms, i.e. it was registered late, which is why date-ordered searches missed it. No residence is given (so Torņakalns is not confirmed here).
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] godparents are a Sirlaks farm owner David (her uncle Dāvis of Vīstuči) and a Smukul.

cites.title: Toronto (news column)
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Izvadot māc. A. Briedim, 13. oktobrī Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumā apglabāja 9. oktobrī 85 g. vecumā mirušo Emmu Sirlaku. Viņa pārmaiņus dzīvojusi gan ASV, kur paliek divas meitas ar ģimenēm, gan - pēdējos gados - Toronto pie meitas Mirdzas Gailītes un znota - matēmatikas skolotāja Friča Gailīša, kas mira pērngada septembrī. Emma Sirlaka nedaudzu gadu laikā pārcieta vairākas smagas operācijas, amputācijā zaudējot vispirms vienu, bet pirms diviem gadiem arī otru kāju.
cites.translation: With Rev. A. Briedis officiating, Emma Sirlaka, who died on 9 October aged 85, was buried on 13 October in the Latvian section of York Cemetery. She had lived alternately in the USA, where two daughters survive with their families, and, in recent years, in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law, the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis, who died last September. Within a few years Emma Sirlaka underwent several serious operations, losing first one leg and, two years ago, the other to amputation.
cites.note: Aged 85, so born about 1885. She spent her old age alternately in the USA, where two of her daughters lived with their families, and (latterly) in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law Fricis Gailītis, a mathematics teacher who died in September 1969. She had had both legs amputated over the preceding years.
cites.why: Two independent notices; [DNA evidence (private)]

cites.title: Phillis May Barns, 5 May 1916
cites.repository: FamilySearch (WA Dept. of Health statewide birth index, filmed)
cites.locator: DGS 101140005 image 721, rec. 76; DGS 101140006 image 586, rec. 7
cites.quote: 652 Barns, Irene (M) Phillis May Barns (C) Seattle John Smith (F) 5-5-16 F W 1763 | 530 Smith, John Phillis May Barns Seattle Irene Barns 5-5-16 F W 1743
cites.note: State birth index, two cards. (1) Filed under the mother: '652 Barns, Irene (M) / Phillis May Barns (C) | Seattle / John Smith (F) | 5-5-16 F W | 1763'. (2) Filed under the father: '530 Smith, John / Phillis May Barns | Seattle / Irene Barns | 5-5-16 F W | 1743'. Seattle certificate no. 1743 or 1763: the two cards disagree. Card 2 is clearer and reads 1743 (my reading; Claude Opus on a tight crop: 1, 7, 4 high certainty, final 3 moderate). Card 1 is blurred; my reading, two independent Claude Haiku passes and Claude Opus all give 1763.
cites.why: Proposed as Estella's ORIGINAL birth record. Same day and city. The child is named 'Phyllis May', and Estella was known as 'Phyllis' and had May as her middle name. The record is illegitimate in form: the child has the mother's surname and the father is the placeholder 'John Smith'. It is the only one of the 169 female entries for 3–7 May 1916 statewide that fits. Not proven until the certificate is seen.
cites.as_recorded: Phillis May Barns (child); Irene Barns (mother); John Smith (father)

cites.title: Estella - Newman - Alderson - Et Al.
cites.repository: Washington State Archives, Digital Archives
cites.quote: Estella May Alderson ... Female ... May 5, 1916 ... Seattle ... King ... Winter Scott Alderson ... Carrie May Newman ... * Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated. ** Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth. ... I certify that no prior certificate has been found for this registrant ... Filed at Seattle, Washington, on April 7, 1952
cites.note: Delayed certificate filed 7 Apr 1952 (Vol. 26, State File No. 342). It names Winter Scott Alderson (b. Oregon, age 50) and Carrie May Newman (b. New York, age 38) as parents. Supporting evidence: (1) affidavit of Carrie May Schroeder, 1952, 'Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated'; (2) affidavit of Mrs. Lola Webster, 25 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth'; (3) Portland Public Schools transcript, 1922–1923 ('Scott Alderson', 'May Alderson'). Registrar's certification: 'no prior certificate has been found for this registrant'. Signed by Estella May Hall, sworn at Portland, 13 Mar 1952.
cites.why: Primary document for date and place. It agrees with every census (b. Washington) and with the SSDI (5 May 1916). The parentage in it rests on the adoptive family's own affidavits, and the registrar found no original certificate under the Alderson name. That is what an original filed under another name would produce.

cites.title: Certificate of Live Birth: Phillis May Barns
cites.repository: Washington State Department of Health, Center for Health Statistics
cites.quote: PHILLIS MAY / BARNS / MAY 05, 1916 04:30 AM / SEATTLE, KING COUNTY, WASHINGTON / IRENE BARNS / WASHINGTON / 18 YEARS / JOHN SMITH / WASHINGTON / 20 YEARS / MAY 12, 1916
cites.note: Original birth certificate, state file no. 146-1916-005906, filed 12 May 1916: Phillis May Barns, female, born 5 May 1916 at 4:30 am, Seattle; facility unknown. Mother 'Irene Barns', born Washington, age 18. Father 'John Smith', born Washington, age 20. The state still issues it in the birth name (never amended for an adoption). See certificate-1916.md.
cites.why: The state's own abstract of the original 1916 certificate. It confirms the index entry on every point, and that Estella = Phillis May Barns: same date and city, and the only fitting birth. The mother's birthplace (Washington) fits Irene Mary Barnhart (b. Lynden WA 1900) and rules against the Barnes alternatives (b. MN, OR). The age (18) overstates Irene Barnhart's 15.

cites.title: Toronto (news column)
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Izvadot māc. A. Briedim, 13. oktobrī Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumā apglabāja 9. oktobrī 85 g. vecumā mirušo Emmu Sirlaku. Viņa pārmaiņus dzīvojusi gan ASV, kur paliek divas meitas ar ģimenēm, gan - pēdējos gados - Toronto pie meitas Mirdzas Gailītes un znota - matēmatikas skolotāja Friča Gailīša, kas mira pērngada septembrī. Emma Sirlaka nedaudzu gadu laikā pārcieta vairākas smagas operācijas, amputācijā zaudējot vispirms vienu, bet pirms diviem gadiem arī otru kāju.
cites.translation: With Rev. A. Briedis officiating, Emma Sirlaka, who died on 9 October aged 85, was buried on 13 October in the Latvian section of York Cemetery. She had lived alternately in the USA, where two daughters survive with their families, and, in recent years, in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law, the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis, who died last September. Within a few years Emma Sirlaka underwent several serious operations, losing first one leg and, two years ago, the other to amputation.
cites.note: Aged 85, so born about 1885. She spent her old age alternately in the USA, where two of her daughters lived with their families, and (latterly) in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law Fricis Gailītis, a mathematics teacher who died in September 1969. She had had both legs amputated over the preceding years.
cites.why: Two independent notices; [DNA evidence (private)]

notes: Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (2026) gives died 1968 and married Mirdza in 1956; ours: died Sep 1969 (Laiks, Oct 1970), married May 1955, Toronto. Lead mh-gailitis-dates.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. / 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. / 3. Dahw | 25½.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now; 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28, 35; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2; 3. Dāvis, 25½.
cites.note: The 1857 soul revision's column for the last revision (1850), XIX Gibboi farm, family 10: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi' 34½, '2. Jahn' 28, '3. Dahw' 25½ (so b. c. 1816, 1822 and 1824/25): the sons of a Jahn, on this farm in 1850. Dahw has no age for 1857; the note beside him reads roughly 'by order of the Kameralhof of 18[?] … 1856, No. 652, transferred to Riga' [?]. The 1850 revision itself (f. 199/1/112) has not been read for this farm.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3). The three are the sons Mārcis (b. 1816), Jānis (b. 1822) and Dāvis (b. 1825) of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847) × Masche in Raimonds's tree: the father's name and all three ages agree. The page names no mother.
cites.as_recorded: Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi, 2. Jahn, 3. Dahw

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. ‖ dessen Frau Anne | 21. / Tochter Anne | 5.
cites.translation: 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28 then, 35 now; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2. His wife Anne, 21; daughter Anne, 5.
cites.note: 1857 soul revision, family 10/58, XIX Gibboi farm, under 'Jahns Söhne': '2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?]' (farmer's assistant[?]), 28 at the last revision (1850), now 35 (b. c. 1822); 'dessen Sohn Marz, 1855 nachgeboren, 2' (his son Mārcis, b. 1855); 'dessen Frau Anne', 21 (b. c. 1836). With them his brother Mārcis, the farmer (41½), and 'Tochter Anne', 5, entered after Jahn's wife. Raimonds's tree has Jānis b. 1822 and his wife Anna b. 1829: her age here does not fit 1829, so she is a second wife or the tree's year is off.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3); high for Jahn (Raimonds's Jānis b. 1822, son of Jānis: age and father agree), medium for his wife: the tree's Anna b. 1829 is seven years older than this Anne.
cites.as_recorded: 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?]; dessen Sohn Marz; dessen Frau Anne

cites.title: Velta Grislis, 19 September 1918 – 12 March 2015
cites.repository: Dignity Memorial (Hulse & English Funeral Home, St. Catharines)
cites.quote: Grislis, Velta. Peacefully on Thursday, March 12th, 2015 at Tufford Manor Nursing Home in her 97th year. Velta, beloved wife of the late Janis. Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family.
cites.note: Born 19 Sep 1918; in her 97th year. 'Beloved wife of the late Janis' (Jānis Grīslis, 11 Mar 1916 – 1 Apr 2012, per a Dignity Memorial index; Timenote gives d. 01.04.2012). 'Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family': relationship not stated, a living third party. The obituary does not name her parents, but Timenote names her father Dāvis and maiden name Sirlaka, and gives her burial at Jaunrauna cemetery (ashes presumably returned to Latvia). She was a Red Cross-trained nurse: there is a 1955 file 'Grislis, Velta (Nee Sirlaks)' in the International Council of Nurses Nurse Refugee Files at the University of Pennsylvania, and Sirlaks hits in the Latvian Red Cross nurses' journal (Žēlsirdīgā Māsa, 1939–40). Her full name was Velta Skaidrīte.

hypotheses.claim: residence 1869 Kalna Vīstuči farm, Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof), Rauna parish, Cēsis district (now Priekuļi parish, Latvia): Purchase of the farm (later "Kalna Vīstuči") from Mārcis Vīstucis, with loans from rich relatives in Liepa parish. "Brāļa Jāņa māja- “Kalna Vīstuči”, brāļa Mārča- “Lejas Vīstuči”, vēlākā Dāvja māja." The farm name comes from the Vīstucis family; Mārcis Sirlaks’s wife Anne was the widow of a Vīstucs (1858 revision).

evidence_for.note: Oral tradition from Emīlis; the 1872 purchase by Pēteris (p. 4, 34) may concern the other half (Lejas Vīstuči).

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (W): Purchase of Kalna Vīstuči (1869, from Mārcis Vīstucis) and Lejas Vīstuči (1872, from von Pander, on instalments). Who was Mārcis Vīstucis relative to Anne’s first husband and her son Dāvis Vīstucs (1858)?

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Jaunrauna manor sale contracts / Cēsis district land books (LVVA); revisions 1850/1858.

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (W): A THIRD brother: the 1834 revision gives the weaver Jahn Sillak’s 1st son Dawe (b. c. 1815/16), who moved to the Lindenhof estate in 1829. Aina knows only Mārcis and Jānis. Was Dāvis the source of the "rich relatives in Liepa" (p. 4)? Lindenhof = Liepa manor.

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Liepa (Lindenhof) revisions 1834/1850; Liepa/Rauna church books for a Dahw/Dawe Sirlak(s).

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (W): Aina lists only three children of Jānis and Līze (1860, 1862, 1866). The passport index has Natālija Zelma Sirlaka, f. Jānis, b. 31 Dec 1893, domicile Jaunrauna: her father must be another Jānis, perhaps an unlisted son of Jānis and Līze.

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Rauna baptisms 1856–1880 (children of Jānis and Līze) and 1893–94 (Natālija Zelma).

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (S): Baptisms of Jānis and Līze's children: Ernestīne 1860 ('Glāznieki'), Reinholds 1862 and Minna 1866 (Jāņmuiža mill). The places point to Cēsis rural parish (Glāznieki; Jāņmuiža/Johannenhof) rather than Rauna; proves the Kalna Vīstuči line.

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Raduraksti: Cēsis (Wenden) Latvian/rural baptisms 1860, 1862, 1866; Rauna baptisms as fallback. (Lead from the alternate draft, research/aina-memoir/alt/.)

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (S): Deaths of Jānis Sirlaks (20.II.1901) and Līze Sirlaka (24.XII.1901). Register entries give ages and birthplaces; the cross dates are probably Julian.

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Raduraksti: Rauna deaths 1901; photograph of the cast-iron cross, Jaunrauna cemetery. (Lead from the alternate draft, research/aina-memoir/alt/.)

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (M): Purchase of Vīstuči: 1869 (Jānis, from 'Mārcis Vīstucis') and 1872 (Pēteris, from von Pander, on instalments); the 16.IV.1915 division act. Contracts and land-book folios would settle the two stories, the split into Kalna/Lejas Vīstuči and the heirs' shares. The alternate draft also cites a division act of 16.IV.1915; that date is not in the memoir text and its source is unknown.

cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1816, manor people
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 31 (fol. 26); farm 29 on image 54 (fol. 49)
cites.quote: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29 | 32. | 37. / Sohn Dawe, nachhergeboren | ½ — Jahns Eheweib Masche, Ansch T. 41
cites.translation: Weaver Jahn, son of Ansis, from no. 29, 32 [in 1811], 37 [now]; son Dāvis, born since, ½. Jahn's wife Masche, daughter of Ansis, 41.
cites.note: 1816 revision (7th), manor people: weaver Jahn, son of Ansch (Ansis), from farm no. 29, aged 32 in 1811 and 37 in 1816 (b. c. 1779); son Dawe, born after 1811, ½. Wife Masche, daughter of Ansch, 41 (b. c. 1775); daughters Trine 16, Anne 14, Marri 10, Liese 5. No surname yet (surnames were assigned in Livonia c. 1822–1826). Also on farm 29 (image 54): farmhand Jahn son of Ansch 'in B', son Peter d. 1814; and young Jahn son of Ansch 'in No. 20'. Died 1830[?] per the 1834 list.
cites.why: Identification with the 1834 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber' rests on the same name and patronymic, a wife Masche daughter of Ansch in both lists (41 → 59, exactly +18 years), son Dawe born after 1811, the trade (weaver) and origin farm 29. Without a surname, a second Jahn son of Ansch on the same estate leaves some doubt.
cites.as_recorded: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29

cites.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998
cites.repository: family papers (Raimonds Voroņins, 2026-10-24)
cites.locator: p. 9, section "PAR PĒTERA UN MARIJAS SESTO BĒRNU KRISTĪNI"
cites.quote: Un atzīme, ka kristīta tā paša gada otrās Lieldienās 25.aprīlī.
cites.translation: And a note that she was baptised on the second day of Easter of the same year, 25 April.
cites.note: Julian Easter 1888 fell on 24 April, so Easter Monday = 25 April Julian (= 7 May Gregorian). This proves Aina copied Julian church-book dates. "Par Kristīni tuvāku ziņu nav." In 1919 she ran across the meadows to Liepa to tell the Latvian army where the Germans were and was given a silver thaler (p. 9).
cites.why: Internally consistent with the Julian Easter of 1888: the note was clearly copied from a church-book entry.

cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. / 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. / 3. Dahw | 25½.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now; 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28, 35; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2; 3. Dāvis, 25½.
cites.note: The 1857 soul revision's column for the last revision (1850), XIX Gibboi farm, family 10: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi' 34½, '2. Jahn' 28, '3. Dahw' 25½ (so b. c. 1816, 1822 and 1824/25): the sons of a Jahn, on this farm in 1850. Dahw has no age for 1857; the note beside him reads roughly 'by order of the Kameralhof of 18[?] … 1856, No. 652, transferred to Riga' [?]. The 1850 revision itself (f. 199/1/112) has not been read for this farm.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3). The three are the sons Mārcis (b. 1816), Jānis (b. 1822) and Dāvis (b. 1825) of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847) × Masche in Raimonds's tree: the father's name and all three ages agree. The page names no mother.

cites.note: 1857 soul revision, family 10/58, XIX Gibboi farm: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth' (Jahn's son Mārcis, the farmer, head of the farm), 34½ at the last revision (1850), now 41½ (b. c. 1816); 'dessen Frau Anne', 38 (b. c. 1819). With them: his brothers 2. Jahn (35; wife Anne 21; son Marz b. 1855) and 3. Dahw (25½ in 1850, gone by 1857), and 'Tochter Anne', 5 (b. c. 1852), entered after Jahn's wife, so the page leaves open whether she is Mārcis's daughter or Jahn's. No Marija: Marija Gibboja (b. 1853) is 'Marri, 4' in the Rauguļi household of the other Marz Gibboi, 50 (image 16).
cites.why: Read at full size, both pages (Round 3). Mārcis, Jahn's son, 41½, is the Mārcis Ģibols b. 1816, son of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847), of Raimonds's tree: age and father agree. His wife Anne, 38, is the Anna b. 1819 whom the tree calls Anna Balodis (the surname is the tree's alone).

cites.quote: [August] — sechsten Morg. 8 Uhr | — sechzehnten | 149. Freudenberg K. Pohdis. Marie Gibboij. Lett. Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. W. Anne, luth. T. Lej Pohdis Jehkabs Pohdis u. s. W. Lihse, K. Pohdis Marie Bitte.
cites.translation: Born [August] the sixth, 8 a.m.; baptised the sixteenth. No. 149. Freudenberg, Upper Pohdis farm. Marie Gibboy. [Parents:] Latvian farmhand Mārcis Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutheran. Godparents: from Lower Pohdis, Jēkabs Pohdis and his wife Līze; from Upper Pohdis, Marie Bitte.
cites.note: Born 6 Aug 1853 Julian (= 18 Aug 1853 Gregorian) at 8 a.m.; baptised 16 Aug 1853. Daughter of Latvian farmhand (Kn. = Knecht) Mahrzis (Mārcis) Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutherans (mother by given name only, as usual in 1853). Godparents: Jehkabs Pohdis and his wife Lihse of Lejas-Pohdis, and Marie Bitte[?] of Kalna-Pohdis. The 71st legitimate girl of the year. The same volume shows a farm named 'Gibboy' on Freudenberg (marriages 1853 no. 21), the likely origin of the surname, and the death of an unmarried maidservant Masche Gibboy, aged 58⅔, at Freudenberg Lejas-Dauksche (deaths 1853 no. 154). Kristīne Gibboy, Marie's probable sister and godmother of Mārtiņš Sirlaks in 1883, should be among later Freudenberg births (Cēsis rural Dz 1847–1879, LVVA 235/7/104).
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] Verified on the crop. Not formally linked to the 1874 bride by a stated age or parents, so 'high' rests on the coincidence of all four details.

Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (2026) makes her the daughter of Mārcis Ģibols (b. 1816, son of Jānis and Masche) and Anna Balodis (b. 1819), married 1843: unsourced, added in 2021. The 1857 Priekuļi soul revision contradicts it: she is 'Marri, 4', daughter of Marz Gibboi (50) and his wife Anne (38) at the Rauguļi farm, with her sister Christine (2), while the 1816 Mārcis is at the Ģiboļi farm with his wife Anne and no Marija. Her parents are Mārcis b. c. 1807 × Anna b. c. 1819, his own 1807 couple (whose 1857 household his note describes), as her 1853 baptism's Mahrzis Gibboy and Anne. His 1816 couple are kept as other people, not linked to her. Lead marija-gibols-parents.

cites.title: Rauna Latvian congregation births and baptisms 1877–1891, 1883 no. 324
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, image 239 (right page)
cites.quote: October, dreißigsten, nachmittags 5 Uhr | sechs u. zwanzigsten | 324. Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz. Martin Wilhelm Sirlak. Elt. Wth Peter Sirlak u. d. Marie geb. Gibboy, beide lutherisch. Pth. Wth Dahw Bitte, Wth Kahrl Sirnis, Md. Kristine Gibboy. Get. vom Past. […] in d. Kirche.
cites.translation: Born 30 October, 5 p.m.; baptised the 26th [December]. No. 324. Neuhof, Lower Vīstuči: Martin Wilhelm Sirlak. Parents: farmer Peter Sirlak and his wife Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmer Dahw Bitte, farmer Kahrl Sirnis, maiden Kristine Gibboy. Baptised by Pastor […] in church.
cites.note: Born 30 Oct 1883 Julian (= 11 Nov 1883 Gregorian), about 5 p.m.; baptised in church 26 Dec 1883 Julian (= 7 Jan 1884 Gregorian). Legitimate son of farmer (Wirth) Peter Sirlak and Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmers Dahw (Dāvis) Bitte and Kahrl Sirnis, and Kristine Gibboy, unmarried (probably Marie's sister; see 1884 no. 315). Last entry of 1883, filed late under December.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] birth Oct 1883 fits death 30 Dec 1942 aged 59; [DNA evidence (private)] 96).

cites.note: Food-goods merchant (pārtikas preču tirgotājs) at the memoir's own address, l. Katrīnas iela 13. The same Cēsis list (p. 436) has 'Smukuls, E., pārtikas tirgot., Palasta ielā 12', a Smukulis food shop (Emma's family?); the branch list on p. 438 has both again, under 'Kolonialpreču tirgotavas' (grocers). The 1927 Cēsu Avīze mentions 'Sirlaka un Smukuļa pārtikas bodes' and 'tirgotājs Sirlaks', one of 'our town's stout men' who walked daily to bathe in the Gauja. Kārlis Krūklītis's memoir recalls the little house on Lielā Katrīnas where 'the well-known Sirlaks' traded for a while. No tea-house (tējnīca) listing found yet.

cites.title: Baznīcas ziņas. Cēsu lauku draudze (in the article run headed 'Patiesības apliecinātāji')
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Baznīcas zinas. Cēsu lauka [sic] draudze. … Miruši: Mārtiņš-Vilhelms Sirlaks, 59 g. v. no Cēsīm, Mārcis Jēkabsons, 80 g. v. no Cēsu Lejas Senčiem …
cites.translation: Church news. Cēsis rural congregation. … Died: Mārtiņš-Vilhelms Sirlaks, aged 59, of Cēsis; Mārcis Jēkabsons, aged 80, …
cites.note: Aged 59, so born about 1883/84. Full name Mārtiņš-Vilhelms. His death is entered in the Cēsis RURAL congregation (Cēsu lauku draudze) news, the same register as Elvīra's 1941 wedding. Funeral 3 Jan 1943 at 2 p.m. from St John's church, Cēsis, to the Lejas kapi (Lower Cemetery), per a family death notice reproduced on Timenote. Timenote gives father Pēteris and birth year 1884. This explains why Mārtiņš was not in the 1944 flight.
cites.why: The church-news entry (name, age, Cēsis) and the family death notice (date, St John's, Lejas kapi) agree; [DNA evidence (private)] Note: the memoir's father 'Mārtiņš' is confirmed as 'Mārtiņš-Vilhelms'.

cites.title: No mums šķīrusies Mirdza Gailīte
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.locator: Laiks, Nr.35 (18.09.2010), p. 22, by Vilis Kalniņš
cites.quote: No mums šķīrusies Mirdza Gailīte (dzirn. [sic: dzim.] Sirlaks) dzimusi 1916. gada 17. janvāri Vidzemes skaistajā pilsētā Cēsis. … Pēc Otrā pasaules kara liktenis ģimeni aizveda uz Kanādu. … Pēc vīra aiziešanas mūžībā kādu laiku dzīvoja Detroitas apkaimē West Bloomfield savā dzīvoklī. Viņa 1990. gada sākumā iestājās Detroitas Daugavas Vanagu apvienībā … Mirdzas divas māsas arī dzīvoja West Bloomfield un Garezera (Long Lake) apkaimē. Pēc aiziešanas pensijā Mirdza Gailīte atgriezās Vindzorā, Kanādā … Mirdza Gailīte aizgāja mūžībā pēkšņi 2010. gada 5. jūlijā. Viņu izvadīja 10. jūlijā no Anderson Funeral Home Vindzorā. Nelaiķe guldīta smilšu kalniņā Toronto.
cites.translation: Mirdza Gailīte (née Sirlaks) has left us. Born 17 January 1916 in the beautiful Vidzeme town of Cēsis. … After the Second World War fate took the family to Canada. … After her husband's death she lived for a while in her apartment in West Bloomfield, near Detroit. In early 1990 she joined the Detroit Daugavas Vanagi branch … Mirdza's two sisters also lived in West Bloomfield and near Garezers (Long Lake). After retiring Mirdza Gailīte returned to Windsor, Canada … She died suddenly on 5 July 2010. The funeral was on 10 July from Anderson Funeral Home, Windsor. She was laid to rest in Toronto.
cites.note: Elvīra's sister. The memoir says Mirdza was born at the rented house in Vinterkalns outside Cēsis, which fits.
cites.why: Obituary; maiden name Sirlaks; Cēsis; two sisters in West Bloomfield and Garezers = Rūta and Elvīra.

cites.title: Raunas latviešu draudzes 1870. gada jūlija–1876. gada dzimušo un kristīto reģistrs, 1875 no. 71
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1875 März | zwei und zwanzigsten, 8¼[?] Uhr abends | eodem die [= neunten] | No. 71. Ronneburg-Neuhof, Lijas Wihstutschi. Natalie Emilie Sirlak. V. Landesbesitzer[?] Peter Sirlak, M. Marrie geb. Gibboy, beide evang. luth. Pathen: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy, Wirth Dahw Bitte sammt[?] Katrihne. gat.[?] in d. Kirche vom Pastor loci.
cites.translation: 1875, March [page]. Born the 22nd [of February], 8:15[?] p.m.; baptised the same day as the entries above (9 March). No. 71. Ronneburg-Neuhof, Greater Vīstuči farm: Natalie Emilie Sirlak. Father: landholder[?] Peter Sirlak; mother: Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: [maid?] Kristine Gibboy, farmer Dahw Bitte with Katrihne. Baptised in the church by the parish pastor.
cites.note: Born [February] 22nd 1875 at 8¼[?] p.m.; baptised 9 March 1875 in the church by the parish pastor (Pastor loci). Parents: farm owner[?] ('Landesbesitzer'[?]) Peter Sirlak and Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy (presumably a Gibbo relative of the mother), farmer (Wirth) Dahw Bitte and [his wife] Katrihne. Rauna Latvian baptisms 1875, no. 71. The birth month is not written on this line; it is carried down from no. 66 ('Februar'). Probably the eldest child, born a year after the Feb 1874 marriage. She is not in the 2015 tree. The farm name shows that 'Lj.' in 1890 = Latvian 'Lielie' (Greater) Vīstuči. 'Wd.', used for another Vīstuči household in 1885, is probably 'Vidus' (Middle).
cites.why: Same parents' names and farm as the 1890 baptism of Anna.

cites.title: Pēteris Sirlaks
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 10.08.1847 Miršanas datums: 10.11.1896 … Tēva vārds: Mārcis … Kapsēta: Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi … Marija Sirlaka — Sieva — 00.00.1853 – 00.00.1925
cites.translation: Born 10 Aug 1847, died 10 Nov 1896; father's name Mārcis; cemetery Jaunrauna (Priekuļi parish); wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925
cites.note: Timenote gives Pēteris Sirlaks 10 Aug 1847 – 10 Nov 1896, son of Mārcis and Anna Sirlaks, buried in Jaunrauna cemetery (Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi). Wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925, NOT 1920 as in the 2015 tree. Children: Natalie 1875–1887, Ernestīne 1879, Mārtiņš 1884–1942, Dāvis 1886–1952, Kristīne 1888, Anna 1890 (the memoir's aunt Anna in Rīga), Augusts 1895. 1938 court notices (Valdības Vēstnesis) mention mortgages issued by a Pēteris Sirlaks, with inheritance shares under a 16 Apr 1915 division act going to Augusts, Ernestīne and Anna Sirlaks. Very likely the same family's farm, which would place the estate division in 1915. PROBABLE SOURCE OF THE 2015 DATES: MyHeritage 'Jurcins Web Site' by Māris Jurciņš (Latvia), whose public name index spells her 'Marija Sirlaka (Ģībojs)', 'Marija Gilboy' and 'Gibboja (Ģībojs)'. 'Gibboja' is exactly the 2015 tree's spelling. Peter emailed himself 'Sirlaks myheritage.com genealogy' on 2018-11-16. MyHeritage pages are behind an hCaptcha and were NOT opened. Marija's maiden name 'Ģībojs/Gibboja' should be verified in the Jaunrauna/Rauna church books.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] Both are user trees without a cited record, so they are derivative until checked against the Rauna/Jaunrauna registers (Raduraksti).

cites.title: Pēteris Sirlaks
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 10.08.1847 Miršanas datums: 10.11.1896 … Tēva vārds: Mārcis … Kapsēta: Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi … Marija Sirlaka — Sieva — 00.00.1853 – 00.00.1925
cites.translation: Born 10 Aug 1847, died 10 Nov 1896; father's name Mārcis; cemetery Jaunrauna (Priekuļi parish); wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925
cites.note: Timenote gives Pēteris Sirlaks 10 Aug 1847 – 10 Nov 1896, son of Mārcis and Anna Sirlaks, buried in Jaunrauna cemetery (Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi). Wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925, NOT 1920 as in the 2015 tree. Children: Natalie 1875–1887, Ernestīne 1879, Mārtiņš 1884–1942, Dāvis 1886–1952, Kristīne 1888, Anna 1890 (the memoir's aunt Anna in Rīga), Augusts 1895. 1938 court notices (Valdības Vēstnesis) mention mortgages issued by a Pēteris Sirlaks, with inheritance shares under a 16 Apr 1915 division act going to Augusts, Ernestīne and Anna Sirlaks. Very likely the same family's farm, which would place the estate division in 1915. PROBABLE SOURCE OF THE 2015 DATES: MyHeritage 'Jurcins Web Site' by Māris Jurciņš (Latvia), whose public name index spells her 'Marija Sirlaka (Ģībojs)', 'Marija Gilboy' and 'Gibboja (Ģībojs)'. 'Gibboja' is exactly the 2015 tree's spelling. Peter emailed himself 'Sirlaks myheritage.com genealogy' on 2018-11-16. MyHeritage pages are behind an hCaptcha and were NOT opened. Marija's maiden name 'Ģībojs/Gibboja' should be verified in the Jaunrauna/Rauna church books.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] Both are user trees without a cited record, so they are derivative until checked against the Rauna/Jaunrauna registers (Raduraksti).

cites.title: Raunas latviešu draudzes 1840.–1850. gada jūnija dzimušo un kristīto reģistrs, 1847 no. 191
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1847 | August [struck word] zehnten[?] Mittags (margin: 10.) | August ein und dreißigsten | No. 191. Neuhof Wihstuz Peter Sirlakk. Elt. Wt. Mahrz Sirlakk, Wtt.[?] Anne. Tfz.[?] 1, Gahles Br.[?] Dahw Sirne 2, desselb. Wb. Lihse Sirne 3, Hof[?] Jug. Dahw Sirlakk. In der Kirche vom Schulmeister[?] Gaike[?]
cites.translation: 1847. Born August the 10th, at midday; baptised August 31st. No. 191. Neuhof, Vīstuči farm: Peter Sirlakk. Parents: farmer Mahrz Sirlakk, [wife] Anne. Godparents: 1. Dahw Sirne of Gahles[?]; 2. his wife Lihse Sirne; 3. bachelor Dahw Sirlakk of Hof[?]. [Baptised] in the church by schoolmaster[?] Gaike[?].
cites.note: Born 10 Aug 1847 (Julian; = 22 Aug Gregorian) at midday; baptised 31 Aug 1847 in the church by the schoolmaster[?] Gaike[?]. Parents: farmer (Wt.) Mahrz [Mārcis/Mārtiņš] Sirlakk and Anne. Godparents: Dahw Sirne of Gahles[?] farm; his wife Lihse Sirne; bachelor (Jug.) Dahw Sirlakk of Hof[?]. Rauna Latvian baptisms 1847, no. 191. The day was first written as another word (struck through) and corrected, with '10.' in the margin.
cites.why: Same name, farm and parish as the 1896 death, whose age (49 y 3 m on 10 Nov 1896) gives exactly Aug 1847. The 1858 revision (below) has Peter aged 10, son of Marz, at the Vīstuči farm.

cites.title: Aina Jurciņa
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.title: Velta Grislis, 19 September 1918 – 12 March 2015
cites.repository: Dignity Memorial (Hulse & English Funeral Home, St. Catharines)
cites.quote: Grislis, Velta. Peacefully on Thursday, March 12th, 2015 at Tufford Manor Nursing Home in her 97th year. Velta, beloved wife of the late Janis. Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family.
cites.note: Born 19 Sep 1918; in her 97th year. 'Beloved wife of the late Janis' (Jānis Grīslis, 11 Mar 1916 – 1 Apr 2012, per a Dignity Memorial index; Timenote gives d. 01.04.2012). 'Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family': relationship not stated, a living third party. The obituary does not name her parents, but Timenote names her father Dāvis and maiden name Sirlaka, and gives her burial at Jaunrauna cemetery (ashes presumably returned to Latvia). She was a Red Cross-trained nurse: there is a 1955 file 'Grislis, Velta (Nee Sirlaks)' in the International Council of Nurses Nurse Refugee Files at the University of Pennsylvania, and Sirlaks hits in the Latvian Red Cross nurses' journal (Žēlsirdīgā Māsa, 1939–40). Her full name was Velta Skaidrīte.

cites.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998
cites.repository: family papers (Raimonds Voroņins, 2026-10-24)
cites.quote: Izvadījām no “Vīstuču” klēts uz Salacu. “Ļekunkās” bēru mielasts. … Kapsēta Salacgrīvas jūras krastā.
cites.translation: We carried her out from the Vīstuči granary to Salaca. Funeral meal at "Ļekunkas". … The cemetery on the seashore at Salacgrīva.
cites.note: Buried at Salacgrīva; funeral meal at the Āboltiņš farm "Ļekunkas". She had earlier ordered a large black marble monument in Cēsis, carried to Salaca by the Vīstuči horses (p. 28) — presumably for the Āboltiņš family grave.
cites.why: Aina attended.

notes: Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (I69), his note: «https://raduraksti.arhivi.lv/objects/1:4:11:2055:2487:24479#&gid=1&pid=23 dzimusi Apiņos, Vecsalacā»

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (M): 'Ļekunkas' farm, Salaca (the Āboltiņš home, bought out with Alma's savings); Zelma Martinsone's grave at Salacgrīva seaside cemetery (d. c. 1960); the black marble monument at Salaca. The family grave probably names Ancis, Dārta and Zelma.

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Salacgrīva cemetery register; BillionGraves/timenote; Salaca land records. (Lead from the alternate draft, research/aina-memoir/alt/.)

sources.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998

hypotheses.claim: other: LEAD (W): Zelma Āboltiņa × widower Aleksandrs Martinsons (drowned); his children Austra and Roberts. Completes Alma's sister's line.

evidence_for.note: Would be settled by: Salaca marriages and deaths (1920s); civil registers. (Lead from the alternate draft, research/aina-memoir/alt/.)

cites.quote: October, dreißigsten, nachmittags 5 Uhr | sechs u. zwanzigsten | 324. Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz. Martin Wilhelm Sirlak. Elt. Wth Peter Sirlak u. d. Marie geb. Gibboy, beide lutherisch. Pth. Wth Dahw Bitte, Wth Kahrl Sirnis, Md. Kristine Gibboy. Get. vom Past. […] in d. Kirche.
cites.translation: Born 30 October, 5 p.m.; baptised the 26th [December]. No. 324. Neuhof, Lower Vīstuči: Martin Wilhelm Sirlak. Parents: farmer Peter Sirlak and his wife Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmer Dahw Bitte, farmer Kahrl Sirnis, maiden Kristine Gibboy. Baptised by Pastor […] in church.
cites.note: Born 30 Oct 1883 Julian (= 11 Nov 1883 Gregorian), about 5 p.m.; baptised in church 26 Dec 1883 Julian (= 7 Jan 1884 Gregorian). Legitimate son of farmer (Wirth) Peter Sirlak and Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmers Dahw (Dāvis) Bitte and Kahrl Sirnis, and Kristine Gibboy, unmarried (probably Marie's sister; see 1884 no. 315). Last entry of 1883, filed late under December.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] birth Oct 1883 fits death 30 Dec 1942 aged 59; [DNA evidence (private)] 96).

cites.title: Rīga St Martin Latvian marriages 1911, no. 34 (summary list; main register no. 62)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 3036, apr. 4, l. 66, image 105 (left page, fol. 98v)
cites.quote: Бракомъ сочетавшіеся въ 1911 году. | 34 | Апрѣля двадцать второго | Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Зирлакъ сынъ Петра (Martin Wilhelm Sirlak) / Эрна Смукулъ, дочь Дава (Erna Smukul) | 62
cites.translation: Married in 1911. No. 34, 22 April: Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, son of Pēteris; Erna [Emma] Smukul, daughter of Dāvis. Main register no. 62.
cites.note: Married 22 Apr 1911 Julian (= 5 May 1911 Gregorian). Groom Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, son of Pēteris; bride written 'Erna' (Эрна / Erna) Smukul, daughter of Dāvis (Дава). The register here is only the year's summary list (no., date, names, fathers, and a reference to no. 62 of the main register, which is not in this volume), so no ages, residence, witnesses or banns. 'Erna' is taken as a clerk's slip for Emma: same clerk writes 'Эмма' plainly at no. 27. Confirms Emma's father's name Dāvis (her US SS record: Dāvis Smukuls) and places the marriage eight months before Elvīra's birth, in the same congregation that baptised her. Corrects the memoir's 'married young': he was 27, she 26.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] same congregation as Elvīra's 1912 baptism. Only the bride's given name differs (Erna vs Emma). Verified by the parent on the crop.

cites.title: Raunas latviešu draudzes 1870. gada jūlija–1876. gada dzimušo un kristīto reģistrs, 1875 no. 71
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1875 März | zwei und zwanzigsten, 8¼[?] Uhr abends | eodem die [= neunten] | No. 71. Ronneburg-Neuhof, Lijas Wihstutschi. Natalie Emilie Sirlak. V. Landesbesitzer[?] Peter Sirlak, M. Marrie geb. Gibboy, beide evang. luth. Pathen: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy, Wirth Dahw Bitte sammt[?] Katrihne. gat.[?] in d. Kirche vom Pastor loci.
cites.translation: 1875, March [page]. Born the 22nd [of February], 8:15[?] p.m.; baptised the same day as the entries above (9 March). No. 71. Ronneburg-Neuhof, Greater Vīstuči farm: Natalie Emilie Sirlak. Father: landholder[?] Peter Sirlak; mother: Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: [maid?] Kristine Gibboy, farmer Dahw Bitte with Katrihne. Baptised in the church by the parish pastor.
cites.note: Born [February] 22nd 1875 at 8¼[?] p.m.; baptised 9 March 1875 in the church by the parish pastor (Pastor loci). Parents: farm owner[?] ('Landesbesitzer'[?]) Peter Sirlak and Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy (presumably a Gibbo relative of the mother), farmer (Wirth) Dahw Bitte and [his wife] Katrihne. Rauna Latvian baptisms 1875, no. 71. The birth month is not written on this line; it is carried down from no. 66 ('Februar'). Probably the eldest child, born a year after the Feb 1874 marriage. She is not in the 2015 tree. The farm name shows that 'Lj.' in 1890 = Latvian 'Lielie' (Greater) Vīstuči. 'Wd.', used for another Vīstuči household in 1885, is probably 'Vidus' (Middle).
cites.why: Same parents' names and farm as the 1890 baptism of Anna.

cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 3036, apr. 4, l. 68, image 15 (right page, bottom)
cites.quote: 1911 Декабря двадцать седьмого (27) 7 ч. веч. | 1912 Февраля девятнадцатаго (19) | № 82 | Эльвира Антонія (Elvira Antonie). Род. торговецъ Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Сирлакъ (Sirlak) ев. лют. вѣр. и его жена Эмма, ур. Смукулъ ев. лют. вѣроиспов. Воспр.: Давидъ Сирлакъ, хозяинъ; Анна Смукулъ, дѣв.; Эрнестина Сирлакъ, дѣвица. Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]
cites.translation: Born 27 December 1911, 7 p.m.; baptised 19 February 1912. No. 82. Elvira Antonie. Parents: trader Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Lutheran, and his wife Emma née Smukul, Ev.-Lutheran. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. Baptised [in …] by Pastor Hilde[?].
cites.note: Born 27 Dec 1911 Julian (= 9 Jan 1912 Gregorian) at 7 p.m.; baptised 19 Feb 1912 Julian (= 3 Mar 1912 Gregorian). Full baptismal name Elvira Antonie. Father: trader (торговецъ) Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Luth.; mother: his wife Emma née Smukul (the ending '-улъ' written over a struck-out ending), Ev.-Luth. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner (хозяинъ) [= her uncle Dāvis]; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. The last line, in another hand, reads roughly 'Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]' — baptised [at …] by Pastor Hilde[?]; place uncertain. Entry no. 82 sits among March baptisms, i.e. it was registered late, which is why date-ordered searches missed it. No residence is given (so Torņakalns is not confirmed here).
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] godparents are a Sirlaks farm owner David (her uncle Dāvis of Vīstuči) and a Smukul.

cites.title: FamilySearch Family Tree: Estella May Alderson (L51K-T7N)
cites.repository: FamilySearch Family Tree (collaborative; read-only pull 2026-10-21)
cites.note: On FamilySearch, Estella (L51K-T7N) is linked to Winter Scott Alderson (L51K-5YQ) and Carrie May Newman (KGWM-KQ2) through relationship MBV4-L65, which has NO lineage type: it is not marked Adoptive and not Biological. The family says she was adopted. Every FamilySearch ancestor of Peter beyond generation 5, about 1,300 people back to the 1200s (Alderson, Royal, Newman, Brate, Cheesman, Stringham, Halsted, Schaeffer, English and Swedish gentry), therefore runs through her ADOPTIVE parents. Peter's biological lines on FamilySearch end at generation 3 (Danenbergs/Sirlaka) and generation 5 (Peter Hall, Peter McCabe: names only).
cites.why: Read directly from GET /platform/tree/child-and-parents-relationships/MBV4-L65 (raw/relationships/MBV4-L65.json).

cites.title: Estella - Newman - Alderson - Et Al.
cites.repository: Washington State Archives, Digital Archives
cites.quote: Estella May Alderson ... Female ... May 5, 1916 ... Seattle ... King ... Winter Scott Alderson ... Carrie May Newman ... * Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated. ** Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth. ... I certify that no prior certificate has been found for this registrant ... Filed at Seattle, Washington, on April 7, 1952
cites.note: Delayed certificate filed 7 Apr 1952 (Vol. 26, State File No. 342). It names Winter Scott Alderson (b. Oregon, age 50) and Carrie May Newman (b. New York, age 38) as parents. Supporting evidence: (1) affidavit of Carrie May Schroeder, 1952, 'Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated'; (2) affidavit of Mrs. Lola Webster, 25 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth'; (3) Portland Public Schools transcript, 1922–1923 ('Scott Alderson', 'May Alderson'). Registrar's certification: 'no prior certificate has been found for this registrant'. Signed by Estella May Hall, sworn at Portland, 13 Mar 1952.
cites.why: Primary document for date and place. It agrees with every census (b. Washington) and with the SSDI (5 May 1916). The parentage in it rests on the adoptive family's own affidavits, and the registrar found no original certificate under the Alderson name. That is what an original filed under another name would produce.

cites.title: Changes of Names and Adoptions
cites.repository: HathiTrust (Univ. of California copy)
cites.note: No Oregon court adoption of Estella is published. The 'Changes of Names and Adoptions' lists printed in the Oregon Laws were read for 1914–1916 (1917 volume) and 1917–1918 (1919 volume). They contain no Alderson as adopter and no 'Phillis', 'Barns' or 'Estella' as a former name. By law, county judges reported every adoption to the Secretary of State for these lists through 1918.
cites.why: These are full, alphabetical, county-by-county lists, and the Alderson slot (between Adams and Allenback in 1917, Adams and Alkire in 1916) is empty. Caveats: the scan is OCR text, some courts reported late or not at all, and an adoption in 1919 or later would fall in the post-1920 ODHS era.

cites.title: S-fs-MLY2-9PZ
cites.repository: FamilySearch / NARA T624
cites.quote: Alderson, Winter S. | Head | M W 43 M1 18 ... May C. | Wife | F W 33 M1 18 | 2 | 2 | New York
cites.note: 1910 census, ED 37, sheet 8A, lines 1–5. Winter S. (43) and May C. (33), married 18 years; she is 'mother of 2 children, 2 living'. The children are Lola L. (17, b. Oregon) and Elmer E. cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1834, farm XXIX Leis Sparing, family 4
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 4. Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber[?] | aus Hofsleute[?] | 1830[?] gestorben / dessen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof[?] / " 2 " Marz | nachhergeboren | | 12. / " 3 " Jahn | nachgeboren | | 4. — Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, dessen Frau | 59.
cites.translation: Jahn Sillak, son of Ansis, manor weaver, from the manor people, died 1830; his 1st son Dāvis, moved 1829 to Lindenhof estate; 2nd son Mārcis, born since the last revision, 12; 3rd son Jānis, born since, 4. Masche Sillak, daughter of Ansis, his wife, 59.
cites.note: 1834 revision (8th), farm XXIX Leis Sparing, family 4: 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber[?]' — died 1830[?] (digit overwritten; possibly 1828); his 1st son Dawe, moved 1829 to the estate Lindenhof[?]; 2nd son Marz, born after 1816, 12 (b. c. 1822); 3rd son Jahn, born after 1816, 4. Female side: 'Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, dessen Frau', 59. Earliest appearance of the surname (as Sillak); Mārcis was the son of Jahn and Masche.
cites.why: Name, father Jahn, brother Jahn (20 in 1850 under the same family), farm XXIX matching the 1850 'aus No. XXIX', and age 12 → 28 all agree. Read by a sub-agent; not re-read by the parent. Masche's age (59, so c. 47 at Mārcis's birth) is doubtful.

cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1816, manor people
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 31 (fol. 26); farm 29 on image 54 (fol. 49)
cites.quote: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29 | 32. | 37. / Sohn Dawe, nachhergeboren | ½ — Jahns Eheweib Masche, Ansch T. 41
cites.translation: Weaver Jahn, son of Ansis, from no. 29, 32 [in 1811], 37 [now]; son Dāvis, born since, ½. Jahn's wife Masche, daughter of Ansis, 41.
cites.note: 1816 revision (7th), manor people: weaver Jahn, son of Ansch (Ansis), from farm no. 29, aged 32 in 1811 and 37 in 1816 (b. c. 1779); son Dawe, born after 1811, ½. Wife Masche, daughter of Ansch, 41 (b. c. 1775); daughters Trine 16, Anne 14, Marri 10, Liese 5. No surname yet (surnames were assigned in Livonia c. 1822–1826). Also on farm 29 (image 54): farmhand Jahn son of Ansch 'in B', son Peter d. 1814; and young Jahn son of Ansch 'in No. 20'. Died 1830[?] per the 1834 list.
cites.why: Identification with the 1834 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber' rests on the same name and patronymic, a wife Masche daughter of Ansch in both lists (41 → 59, exactly +18 years), son Dawe born after 1811, the trade (weaver) and origin farm 29. Without a surname, a second Jahn son of Ansch on the same estate leaves some doubt.
cites.as_recorded: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29

cites.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998
cites.repository: family papers (Raimonds Voroņins, 2026-10-24)
cites.quote: Tajā atrodam Sirlaku senčus: piecas paaudzes atpakaļ tie bija divi brāļi Mārcis un Jānis. No Mārča izveidojās Dāvja, bet no Jāņa- Emīļa dinastijas.
cites.translation: There we find the Sirlaks ancestors: five generations back they were two brothers, Mārcis and Jānis. From Mārcis grew Dāvis’s dynasty, from Jānis Emīlis’s.
cites.note: sibling: brother Jānis Sirlaks (b. 8 May 1829, d. 1901). The memoir’s own table (p. 38) repeats "Mārcis- ---- Jānis- 1829. brāļi".
cites.why: Independently confirmed by the 1834 Jaunrauna revision (data/families/F1001.yaml): in the family of the manor weaver Jahn Sillak (d. 1830[?]) and Masche, the 2nd son Marz is 12 and the 3rd son Jahn 4 (b. c. 1830), on farm XXIX Lejas Spāriņi; Aina’s Jānis was born 8 May 1829 at "Spāriņi" (p. 8). The same revision lists an elder brother Dawe who moved to Lindenhof in 1829, whom Aina does not mention.

cites.translation: 1847. Born August the 10th, at midday; baptised August 31st. No. 191. Neuhof, Vīstuči farm: Peter Sirlakk. Parents: farmer Mahrz Sirlakk, [wife] Anne. Godparents: 1. Dahw Sirne of Gahles[?]; 2. his wife Lihse Sirne; 3. bachelor Dahw Sirlakk of Hof[?]. [Baptised] in the church by schoolmaster[?] Gaike[?].
cites.note: Born 10 Aug 1847 (Julian; = 22 Aug Gregorian) at midday; baptised 31 Aug 1847 in the church by the schoolmaster[?] Gaike[?]. Parents: farmer (Wt.) Mahrz [Mārcis/Mārtiņš] Sirlakk and Anne. cites.translation: Farm No. XIV Vīstuči … family 15/95: Mārcis Sirlaks, son of Jānis, aged 28 at the last revision, 36 now; his stepson[?] Dāvis Vīstucs, 14; son Pēteris Sirlaks, 10. His wife Anne, widow of [a] Vīstucs, 51.
cites.note: 1858 revision list (10th revision), family no. 95 (9th revision no. 15). Marz Sillakk, son of Jahn: aged 28 at the 1850 revision, 36 now (so b. c. 1821/22). His stepson[?] Dahw Wihstuz: 6 → 14. Son Peter Sillakk: 2 → 10. Female side: 'his wife Anne, widowed Wihstuz', 51 (so b. c. 1806/07). So Anne was the widow of a Wihstuz (the farm's earlier family) and Dahw Wihstuz is Peter's older half-brother. Gives Pēteris's grandfather's name, Jānis (Jahn), and the patronymic of Mārcis.
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] 'Sillakk' is the revision clerk's spelling; the family index of the same volume lists it as 'Sillak' (no. 95).

cites.translation: Born [August] the sixth, 8 a.m.; baptised the sixteenth. No. 149. Freudenberg, Upper Pohdis farm. Marie Gibboy. [Parents:] Latvian farmhand Mārcis Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutheran. Godparents: from Lower Pohdis, Jēkabs Pohdis and his wife Līze; from Upper Pohdis, Marie Bitte.
cites.note: Born 6 Aug 1853 Julian (= 18 Aug 1853 Gregorian) at 8 a.m.; baptised 16 Aug 1853. Daughter of Latvian farmhand (Kn. = Knecht) Mahrzis (Mārcis) Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutherans (mother by given name only, as usual in 1853). Godparents: Jehkabs Pohdis and his wife Lihse of Lejas-Pohdis, and Marie Bitte[?] of Kalna-Pohdis. The 71st legitimate girl of the year. The same volume shows a farm named 'Gibboy' on Freudenberg (marriages 1853 no. 21), the likely origin of the surname, and the death of an unmarried maidservant Masche Gibboy, aged 58⅔, at Freudenberg Lejas-Dauksche (deaths 1853 no. 154). Kristīne Gibboy, Marie's probable sister and godmother of Mārtiņš Sirlaks in 1883, should be among later Freudenberg births (Cēsis rural Dz 1847–1879, LVVA 235/7/104).
cites.why: [DNA evidence (private)] Verified on the crop. Not formally linked to the 1874 bride by a stated age or parents, so 'high' rests on the coincidence of all four details.
